newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander 9-mo profit rise lags key competition.
newsitem.headline: Santander 9-mo profit rise lags key competition.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Monday a rise in its nine-month results showed its ambitious Latin American shopping spree was bearing fruit, but profit growth still trailed behind those of its key competitors.

Santander, the nation's largest bank, said its nine-month attributable earnings rose 13.22 percent to 71.78 billion pesetas ($559.5 million), amid a consolidation of its leading domestic position and from foreign operations.
But its earnings growth was outstripped by profits at key competitors.
Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, the nation's second-largest bank, profits rose 26.5 percent in the first nine months on buoyant foreign business, while Banco Central Hispano earnings climbed 20.1 percent.

Santander said it had benefited from foreign business and from strong financial trading results as Spanish markets soared on the belief the nation would join the first wave of European monetary union.
Operating income from abroad jumped 80 percent in the first nine months to 29.41 billion pesetas.

In a letter to shareholders, Chairman Emilio Botin said "These results reflect the excellent evolution of recurrent income generated by the group, which stems from a strategy focused on consolidating its position as the leading financing institution in Spain and taking advantage of opportunities in other markets."

The previously announced merger of Banco Santander Chile with Banco Osorno y La Union took effect on July 1. In Europe, Santander agreed at the beginning of July to buy up to 10 percent of Hungarian bank Inter Europa Bank for $6 million.
Last week, Santander said it would take control of Mexico's Grupo Financiero Invermexico, which owns Banco Mexicano and Invermexico Casa de Bolsa.

Still, the recent purchases ate into earnings under the burden of 10-year amortisations. Without amortisation, profits would have risen 16.2 percent in the period and not 13.22 percent, the bank said.

In the third quarter, the bank had amortisation costs of 5.17 billion pesetas, roughly half of which stemmed from the 1994 purchase of Banesto while the other half stemmed from purchases in Latin America, a bank spokesman said. ($ = 128.2 Spanish Pesetas)
